Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (84 of 84 at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) Restore exactly scoped — confirmed.** In `useAppShellBranding` (`packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx` at head) the capture `previousFaviconHref = link.getAttribute('href')` sits immediately before the write `link.href = branding.favicon`, both inside the same effect body, and the restore is in that effect's returned cleanup behind `if (faviconLink)`. Dependency list: `[branding?.primaryColor, branding?.accentColor, branding?.favicon, title]`. For A→B, React runs A's cleanup (restores pre-A) before B's effect body runs, so B captures pre-A; the final unmount runs B's cleanup and lands on pre-A, not A. Pinned by "switching branding A → B shows B, and the final unmount restores the pre-A icon, not A". No breaking case found: the intermediate no-favicon shape (A → undefined → B, the console's loading state) also ends on pre-A (A's cleanup restores; the undefined run captures nothing; B captures pre-A). Observation only: because the effect also keys on the colour props and `title`, a title-only or colour-only change replays restore-then-branded-write back to back in one synchronous flush; the end state is unchanged and this mirrors the title's existing behaviour.
- **(b) Attribute-vs-property capture — confirmed correct.** `HTMLLinkElement.href` reflects a URL attribute: the getter resolves the content attribute against the document base, so `href=""` (the console's own icon link in `apps/console/index.html`, until the boot script or `main.tsx` writes an operator favicon) reads back as the page URL, and an absent attribute reads back as `""`, collapsing two distinct states. `getAttribute('href')` returns the exact bytes or `null`. Cleanup: `null` → `removeAttribute('href')`; `''` or any string → `setAttribute('href', value)`. Both pinned ("an empty href … comes back empty, not as the page URL"; "an icon link with no href attribute is left with none"). The environment-control test measures that resolution in happy-dom (root `vitest.config.mts`, `environment: 'happy-dom'`) before the pins rely on it. The forward write through the property sets the content attribute to the given string, so write and restore act on the same attribute.
- **(c) No favicon / no icon link — confirmed by reading.** `faviconLink` and `previousFaviconHref` start `null`; both are assigned only inside `if (branding?.favicon)` then `if (link)`; the hook contains no `createElement`; the cleanup's favicon branch is `if (faviconLink)`. Pinned by "a shell with no favicon writes no icon and restores nothing" (which also plants a third-party write during the mount and checks it survives the unmount) and "a page with no icon link gets none — neither on mount nor on unmount".
- **(d) FaviconSync interaction — no fight found.** Tree at head: `apps/console/src/App.tsx` mounts `FaviconSync` as the first child of `BrowserRouter`, ahead of the `UploadProvider` → `ConsoleShell` → `Routes` subtree; the only console consumer of the hook is `packages/app-shell/src/layout/ConsoleLayout.tsx` (layout `AppShell` with `branding={activeApp?.branding …}`) inside that later subtree. Within one commit React (the repo's pinned release, via the root `pnpm.overrides`) runs every passive cleanup before any passive create, whatever the sibling or child placement, so the shell's restore cannot land after a FaviconSync write made in the same commit; among creates, FaviconSync's fires first (earlier, shallower sibling) and the shell's after — the order the dev measured. Across commits (a lazily loaded target route suspending so the old shell's unmount cleanup lands a commit later than FaviconSync's location-keyed write): with an operator favicon O configured, every pre-shell writer (the `index.html` boot script, `main.tsx` before `createRoot().render()`, and FaviconSync's own first effect) writes O, so the captured pre-A value is O and a late restore writes the same URL FaviconSync just wrote; with no operator favicon, FaviconSync never writes (`if (faviconUrl)` gate) and the restore is the only writer. A child placement would only make FaviconSync unmount with the shell, leaving the restore alone. The one divergence is the declared replay caveat (a third-party write while mounted is overwritten on unmount), identical to the title's. The pre-existing in-app-navigation overwrite (FaviconSync writing O over a branded icon on `/apps/a` → `/apps/a/page-2`) is real on both trees and is correctly reported as out of scope.
- **(e) Pins real and able to fail — consistent.** 9 tests (1 environment control + 8 pins) importing `../AppShell` source. Re-deriving the ablation table against the assertions: leg 1 (branch point, no restore) reddens the 5 unmount-restore pins (sentinel, A→B, empty href, absent href, rel-only) and leaves the write pin, no-favicon pin, no-link pin and the control green → 5 failed / 4 passed as reported; leg 2 (property capture) reddens the same 5 (relative sentinel and `''` come back resolved, absent comes back as `''`) → 5 / 4; leg 3 (cleanup writes when nothing was written) reddens only the no-favicon pin → 1 / 8; leg 4 (forward write removed) reddens exactly the 5 tests that assert the branded value while mounted (write pin, A→B, empty, absent, rel-only) and leaves the sentinel-restore pin green because it never asserts the branded state → 5 / 4; leg 5 (create a link) reddens only the no-link pin → 1 / 8. Each of the 8 pins is red in at least one leg; the environment control is red in none, by design.
- **(f) Changeset — every sentence true at head.** The title/favicon asymmetry on the branch point, the FaviconSync gate, the `#favicon` then `link[rel="icon"]` lookup, the attribute capture and `href=""` reasoning, absent-attribute handling, the no-favicon / no-link no-op, no link creation, and the unconditional replay caveat all match the code as read. No line-address citations. One precision note, not a falsehood: "makes two branded writes to the document" counts the two tab-surface writes (title, icon `href`); the same effect also writes brand colour custom properties on the document root, which it removes rather than restores on unmount (as `content/docs/layout/app-shell.mdx` says). The sentence's count is scoped to the surfaces it enumerates.
